editorial:
Imagine you are on a road trip to Las Vegas with a group of friends, just looking for some fun and excitement. You decide to take a detour and stop in a creepy ghost town called Garlock, California. That is exactly where the story starts. You get to watch everything unfold through found footage, which makes you feel like you are right there in the car and on the dusty streets with the eight travelers. The vibe is very uneasy from the start, and you can feel the tension grow as the group realizes they are not alone in this abandoned place.

What really works here is how the movie builds up the mystery. The acting feels natural, and the slow build makes the scares hit harder when they finally happen. While some parts move a bit slowly, the payoff is worth it if you like thrillers that keep you guessing.
endingExplained: The movie ends with a shocking reveal that the group was being hunted by something far more dangerous than they first thought. As the survivors try to escape the ghost town, it becomes clear that they were lured there on purpose. Most of the group dies in a violent scramble, leaving only a few left to face the truth. The final footage cuts off just as the horror reaches its peak, leaving you wondering if anyone actually made it out alive.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves found footage movies and spooky road trip stories.
